A rich heritage, a bright future.
Founded in 1896 by Lex Devine — a visionary ahead of his time — Clayesmore was built on the belief that education should nurture the whole person. Not just the scholar, but the artist, the athlete, the leader, the friend.
Today, that founding ethos remains at our heart. Set within 62 acres of Dorset countryside, we offer an all-through journey from Nursery to Sixth Form, rooted in values that endure and an outlook that's unmistakably modern.

Senior Curriculum
YEAR 9 – YEAR 11
In Year 9 students study English, Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Geography, History, IT, Food and Nutrition, Design Technology, Art and PE. Each week Year 9s also have lessons, taught by senior staff, in debating, presentation skills, conservation and critical thinking. If it is appropriate they will study both French and Spanish. They all play sport three times a week – on Mondays, Thursdays and Saturdays. On Saturdays they have LEX sessions, more details of which can be found here.
In March – April of Year 9 students choose their GCSE Options. Everyone takes English Language, Maths and Science. Most also take English Literature and some also take Further Mathematics.
Students then choose up to 4 additional optional subjects, leading to between 6 and 11 GCSEs.
The optional subjects are: Art and Design, Computer Science, Creative iMedia, Design and Technology, Food Preparation and Nutrition, French, Spanish, Geography, History, Music, PE.
Students who have some learning support usually have their support lessons in place of one or sometimes two optional subjects. This is discussed in detail with parents and pupils.
Science: more able scientists take three separate sciences. Students who find Science less interesting or useful have lessons in all three sciences and take the combined science award.
International students can be prepared for a globally recognised IGCSE in English as a Second Language. Some international students also take a GCSE in their own language if it is offered by the exam board. We have recently had students take a qualification in German, French, Italian, Greek, Mandarin, Japanese and Turkish.

History
A History of Clayesmore
Nestled in the beautiful English countryside, Clayesmore School is centred on an impressive Victorian mansion designed by the celebrated Gothic Revival architect Alfred Waterhouse, best known for creating London’s iconic Natural History Museum. Surrounded by 62 acres of rolling Dorset countryside, the Main House sits within grounds that include expansive sports pitches, mature woodland, and a picturesque lake. The lake, home to swans and visiting wildlife including otters, has become a memorable feature of school life. It is famously incorporated into the school’s cross-country relays and also supports outdoor learning, with an outdoor classroom regularly used by the Prep School for exploration and environmental education.
Clayesmore’s Story
Before becoming a school, the house was originally built as a private residence. One of its most notable owners was James Ismay, son of Thomas Henry Ismay, the founder of the famous shipping company White Star Line, whose vessels included the ill-fated RMS Titanic. The family brought elements of their previous home with them when they moved in. The remarkable fireplace in the main reception room, for example, was transported brick by brick from their former mansion at Dawpool. Today it remains one of the architectural highlights of the house and a fascinating reminder of the building’s earlier history.
Clayesmore’s story as a school began in 1933, when the property was purchased by its visionary founder, Alexander “Lex” Devine. Devine moved his small but ambitious school to the site, bringing with him a progressive educational philosophy that valued character, curiosity, and community. Over the decades that followed, the school grew around the historic house, combining its rich heritage with modern facilities and a vibrant academic and co-curricular life.
Today, Clayesmore’s historic setting continues to shape the experience of its pupils, providing a unique environment where tradition, landscape, and learning come together.

Fee Support / Bursaries
Fee Support and Bursaries
At Clayesmore, we believe that a child’s education should be shaped by their potential, not limited by financial circumstances. We are committed to making a Clayesmore education accessible to bright, curious and enthusiastic children through a range of means-tested fee support options.
Financial assistance is available through means-tested bursaries. Families wishing to apply are invited to complete a bursary application form, which is reviewed confidentially by the School’s Bursary Committee. Bursary awards are tailored to each family’s individual circumstances and are intended to help make a Clayesmore education more accessible. The level of support available varies from case to case and is subject to both financial assessment and the School’s bursary budget. While bursaries can make a significant contribution towards school fees, they are generally intended to provide assistance with the cost of a Clayesmore education rather than full fee remission. Although we endeavour to support as many families as possible, bursary awards cannot be guaranteed in every case.
Sibling Discount
The School offers a 5% fee discount for the eldest sibling on roll and a 10% discount for each subsequent sibling attending the School concurrently. Our Admissions team is always happy to discuss the fee support options available and guide families through the application process.

Immersion Groups
British Boarding School Experience
The Inspired Learning Group offers a British Boarding School Experience across its schools, including Clayesmore School, Shebbear College, Saint Felix School, and St Francis College (girls only), for students aged 10–18.
Our programmes are carefully designed for international students to experience life in a British boarding school. Students are fully integrated into the daily routines at Clayesmore School, providing a genuine insight into school life in the UK. This includes attending lessons, participating in co-curricular activities, and engaging in the wider school community.
Alongside academic learning, students develop their English language skills through real-life interaction, improving their speaking, listening, reading, and writing in a natural and supportive environment. Cultural activities further enrich the experience, helping students gain a deeper understanding of British traditions and lifestyle.
This experience builds confidence, strengthens communication skills, and supports a smooth transition into UK education. It also provides an excellent opportunity for students to form lasting friendships with peers from around the world, broadening their global perspective.
Programmes can run from one week to several weeks and are available for individual families, visiting school groups, and educational agents. As well as being a rewarding experience, this programme offers an ideal introduction for students considering full-time study at one of our schools.
Please click on the links to explore our schools further, or email [email protected] for advice, availability, and bookings.

Scholarships
Scholarships at Clayesmore
At Clayesmore, we celebrate talent, commitment and potential across a wide range of disciplines. Scholarships are available for pupils who demonstrate excellence in Music, Art, Drama, Design and Technology, Sport and Academic achievement.
Prep School Scholarships (Year 7 entry)
Each year, current Year 6 pupils are invited to apply for scholarships for entry into Year 7 at Clayesmore Prep for the following academic year.
Scholarships are awarded on an individual basis and may offer a reduction in fees. Pupils may apply for more than one scholarship, but if successful in multiple areas, will be asked to accept one award. Awards remain in place through to the end of Year 8.
Senior School Scholarships (Year 9 entry)
Pupils progressing from Year 8 into Year 9 are invited to apply for Senior School scholarships. These build on the same areas of excellence and provide an opportunity to continue recognising and developing individual strengths as pupils move into the Senior School.
Sixth Form Scholarships (Year 12 entry)
We also offer scholarships for entry into Year 12, recognising outstanding ability and potential as students begin their Sixth Form studies.
Further Information
Scholarship applications are made during the Autumn Term, with assessments taking place in January.
Full details of each scholarship programme, including application guidance and deadlines, can be found in our brochure below:
We encourage all families to explore these opportunities and to speak with our Admissions team if they would like guidance on the most appropriate pathway for their child.

Admissions
Admissions
The admissions process usually begins with a visit to the nursery, giving families the opportunity to see our setting in action. Nursery tours can also include the Prep School facilities. Full tours of the whole School can be arranged on request.
Following your visit, children are normally invited back for a stay and play session with their parents. Once a place has been accepted, children will take part in a settling-in period, allowing them to become familiar with the nursery environment before their official start date.
To book a tour, please email [email protected] or call 01747 813010.
Information on nursery fees is available on request.
Settling In
All children experience a period of transition when moving from home to nursery, and each child responds in their own way. While some children settle quickly, others may need a little more time. We work closely with families to ensure every child feels supported, safe and secure during this important stage.
We offer a gradual settling-in process, helping children become confident in the nursery environment and reassuring them that parents will always return.
We understand that working parents may need to drop off and go, so we encourage families to plan ahead and, where possible, attend settling-in sessions in the weeks before returning to work. It is also helpful to have another authorised family member available for collection if a child is finding the transition difficult.
We pride ourselves on working openly and flexibly with parents. The wellbeing of each child and their family is always our priority, and we tailor the settling-in process to ensure a positive and successful start to nursery life.

Nursery Heads Welcome
It is a true privilege not only to lead an early years setting, but to have the opportunity to create it from the very beginning. It feels especially meaningful as I spent part of my own childhood growing up in this wonderful village and community that has always held a special place in my heart.
With more than 20 years of experience in early years education, a degree in Childhood Studies and specialist early years qualifications, I am passionate about giving every child the very best start in life. I believe childhood should be filled with wonder, curiosity, kindness and a strong sense of belonging.
At Clayesmore Nursery, every decision has been carefully considered to create an environment where children feel safe, valued and inspired to learn. Our beautiful nursery has been thoughtfully designed to provide calm, nurturing spaces, natural resources and endless opportunities for exploration, creativity and outdoor adventure.
Relationships are at the heart of everything we do. By working closely with families, we create a genuine partnership that supports every child’s unique journey. We celebrate each milestone, nurture confidence and independence, and encourage children to develop a lifelong love of learning through meaningful play and memorable experiences.
My vision is not simply to provide exceptional care and education today, but to create a nursery that leaves a lasting legacy for generations of children and families to come.
As Winnie the Pooh so beautifully said: “We didn’t realise we were making memories, we just knew we were having fun.” Those words perfectly capture what childhood should be.
Hannah Miles Head of Nursery
It is an honour to be part of the Clayesmore community, and I very much look forward to welcoming your family to Clayesmore Nursery as we begin this exciting new chapter together.

Boarding Experience
Boarding at Clayesmore Prep is seriously fun!
Boarding life at Clayesmore Prep School closely resembles the atmosphere and diversity of a busy, loving and happy family, but with the advantage of being surrounded by friends 24 hours a day!
Around 50 girls and boys board with us in Aubrey House and are cared for by devoted Houseparents, Jess Chisholm and Tom Brown, with a team of matrons, nursing staff and tutors, whose focus is to provide a home-from-home environment.
Evenings are spent playing games, swimming, karaoke competitions, baking brownies, watching films, or enjoying barbecues. The children also get to relax and spend time with friends, just like at home. Mobile phone use (if students have access) is carefully monitored to allow calls home at specific times, but not much more.
Sundays are for expeditions, and the children head off to exciting new places every week, such as the coast for beach games, the Haynes Motor Museum, Dorset Water Park, Snowtrax, Monkey World and many other exciting locations.
A Home Away from Home
At Clayesmore, boarding isn’t just about where you sleep—it’s about belonging. We provide a warm, family-style environment where pupils feel supported, safe and empowered to grow. Our boarding culture is built around friendship, independence, and personal development. Pupils are surrounded by trusted adults who care deeply about their welfare and success, and who create a true home away from home.
Types of Boarding
At Clayesmore, we understand that every family’s circumstances are different, which is why we offer a flexible range of boarding options to suit individual needs and lifestyles.
Full Boarding
For pupils staying seven days a week throughout term time, full boarding offers the most immersive Clayesmore experience. Pupils become deeply involved in every aspect of school life—academic, pastoral, co-curricular and social. With structured weekends filled with enriching activities, trips, and time to unwind with friends, full boarders develop strong friendships and a powerful sense of belonging. It’s a wonderful environment for pupils to grow in independence, build resilience, and gain confidence in a secure, supportive setting.
Weekly Boarding
Weekly boarders stay from Monday to Saturday and return home after the end of commitments on Saturdays. This option is ideal for families living within a couple of hours’ drive of the school who want their children to enjoy the structure, community and enrichment of the boarding environment during the school week, while still spending some time at home. Weekly boarding offers the best of both worlds—academic focus and weekday independence, with regular family time.
Flexi Boarding
Flexi boarding offers the ultimate flexibility for modern family life. Pupils can board on specific nights when needed—whether due to long commutes, parental work commitments, school events, or as an introduction to boarding life. This option is perfect for pupils who want to take part in early or late activities, gain a little extra independence, or gradually ease into full-time boarding. Flexi boarders are fully integrated into house life during their stay and benefit from the same warm, supportive environment.
Exeats
Every half term, the school has one exeat weekend. On this weekend, most students will go home after school on Friday and return on Sunday evening. However, international students are able to stay at school for a weekend with a difference. Activities and trips are planned which showcase areas of the UK you may not yet have visited – a trip to London to watch a sports fixture, for example, or a trip to the theatre. The weekend brings our international community closer together and it is valued by the students.
Our Senior Boarding Houses
Clayesmore has six boarding houses—one for prep, three for boys and two for girls—each with its own personality and strong sense of community.
Each house is led by experienced Houseparents, supported by pastoral and academic staff who know every pupil personally.

Learning Support
High academic achievement begins with a deep professional commitment to understanding how children learn.
For more than 25 years, the school has been recognised nationally for its expertise in supporting pupils with dyslexia, dyspraxia, ADHD and other learning differences, and we are proud to hold CReSTeD accreditation. However, what distinguishes Clayesmore is that this expertise shapes teaching and learning across the entire school.
Our work is led by the Deputy Head Academic and the SENCO, supported by a specialist team able to assess pupils carefully and provide detailed guidance for teachers. All teaching and pastoral staff are trained not simply in what children need to learn, but in how children learn effectively. This influences lesson design, classroom routines, revision strategies and approaches to feedback across every subject.
Teachers use explicit instruction, carefully sequenced learning, retrieval practice, collaborative discussion and visual explanation to help pupils develop confidence and independence. The approaches which best support pupils with dyslexia, slower processing or concentration difficulties almost always are the same approaches that improve learning for everyone.
This understanding also shapes the school’s wider expectations and routines. We believe strongly in high standards, while recognising that memory, organisation, executive functioning and attention are skills which need to be taught and reinforced. Expectations remain high, but our responses are always thoughtful, proportionate and educational.
This approach enables a wide range of pupils to succeed. Recent leavers have progressed to Oxford to study Mathematics and English, while former pupils have gone on to complete doctorates at, among many other places, Warwick, Cambridge and Imperial College London.

Curriculum
Our Curriculum
Our Pre-Prep curriculum provides a strong foundation for every child’s educational journey, combining academic excellence with creativity, curiosity and a love of learning.
In Reception, learning follows the Early Years Foundation Stage, where children continue their development through play, exploration and carefully planned experiences. As they move into Years 1 and 2, they begin the Key Stage 1 curriculum, building secure foundations in phonics, reading, writing, mathematics and science. Alongside these core subjects, children explore history, geography, art, design and technology, computing, music, PE and PSHE through engaging, hands-on learning.
We believe children learn best when they are actively involved in their education. Specialist teaching, outdoor learning, Forest School, educational visits and enrichment activities are woven throughout the curriculum, helping pupils make meaningful connections and discover new passions.
Above all, our curriculum is designed to develop confident, curious and compassionate learners. We encourage children to ask questions, solve problems, think independently and work collaboratively, equipping them with the skills, knowledge and confidence to flourish throughout their time at Clayesmore and beyond.

Prep Curriculum
Curriculum Overviews
At Clayesmore Prep School, our curriculum is carefully designed to inspire curiosity, challenge pupils academically and support every stage of their development. As children progress through the school, learning evolves from a nurturing, class-based environment to a more specialist and independent approach, preparing them confidently for senior school and beyond.
Across all year groups, pupils benefit from a broad and balanced curriculum that combines strong academic foundations with creative, practical and experiential learning opportunities. Specialist teaching, outdoor education, enrichment activities and the values of the Clayesmore Compass help pupils develop the knowledge, skills and personal qualities needed to thrive both inside and outside the classroom.
Explore each stage of the Prep School curriculum below to discover how learning develops from Years 3 and 4 through to Year 8.
In Years 3, 4, and 5 children begin their journey through the Prep School with a broad, engaging curriculum designed to build strong foundations in key skills while nurturing curiosity and confidence.
Learning is delivered primarily by a class teacher, ensuring consistency, strong relationships and close pastoral care. As a result, children feel secure and supported as they develop independence and a love of learning.
The curriculum focuses on core skills in English and Mathematics, alongside Science, Humanities, Languages, Creative Arts, Computing, PE and Outdoor Education. Lessons are practical, creative and interactive, encouraging children to explore ideas, ask questions and make connections across subjects.
As well as developing academic skills, pupils begin to build independence through structured prep and are introduced to specialist teaching in areas such as music, PE, computing and languages. Outdoor learning, trips and enrichment activities bring learning to life and help children develop confidence beyond the classroom.
At the heart of learning is the Clayesmore Compass — Communication, Consideration, Creativity and Courage — which helps pupils develop positive attitudes and strong personal foundations for future success.
In Year 6, pupils move into a more specialist teaching model while continuing to benefit from strong pastoral support through their tutor and form system.
This stage marks an important transition as pupils become more independent learners, developing confidence, responsibility and deeper academic understanding across all subjects.
The curriculum builds on strong foundations in English and Mathematics, while introducing greater depth and challenge in Science, Humanities, Languages, Computing and the Creative Arts. Pupils are encouraged to think more critically, work collaboratively and take greater ownership of their learning.
Specialist teaching becomes more frequent, and pupils benefit from a wide range of enrichment opportunities including outdoor education, fieldwork, performances and residential experiences.
Prep becomes a more structured part of learning, helping pupils develop organisation, time management and independent study skills.
The Clayesmore Compass continues to underpin all aspects of school life, supporting pupils in developing communication, creativity, courage and consideration as they prepare for the next stage of their education.
In Year 7, pupils enter Key Stage 3 learning while still within the supportive environment of the Prep School, ensuring a smooth and confident transition towards senior school education.
All subjects are taught by specialist teachers, allowing pupils to explore greater depth and complexity across the curriculum. Learning becomes more analytical and independent, with a strong focus on developing critical thinking, problem-solving and subject-specific skills.
The curriculum includes English, Mathematics, Science, Humanities, Languages, Computing, Creative Arts, PE and PSHRE, with increased emphasis on applying knowledge in more challenging and extended tasks.
Pupils are encouraged to take greater responsibility for their learning, manage their workload effectively and develop resilience and independence in preparation for future academic demands.
Enrichment continues through trips, performances, outdoor learning and leadership opportunities, helping pupils to broaden their experiences and build confidence.
In Year 8, pupils reach the final year of Prep School and are fully prepared for transition into senior school and GCSE study.
The curriculum is challenging, broad and academically ambitious, delivered by specialist teachers who encourage independence, depth of understanding and strong analytical thinking.
Pupils study a wide range of subjects including English, Mathematics, Science, Humanities, Languages, Computing, Creative Arts, PE and PSHRE. Learning focuses on applying knowledge, developing advanced skills and preparing for the expectations of senior school study.
There is a strong emphasis on independent learning, organisation and personal responsibility. Pupils are encouraged to think critically, reflect on their progress and take ownership of their academic development.
Enrichment plays an important role in Year 8, with leadership opportunities, trips, performances and outdoor experiences helping pupils build confidence and maturity.
By the end of Year 8, pupils leave Clayesmore Prep as confident, capable and well-rounded individuals, fully prepared for the next stage of their education.

Senior
Ensuring our pupils feel confident and comfortable in the classroom is at the heart of what we do.
At Clayesmore, we believe students who feel confident and comfortable enough to make mistakes in the classroom are most likely to go on to achieve academic success. Our teachers are skilled practitioners; finding ways to encourage those who are a little shy to take part, providing scaffolding for those who are reluctant to write, and challenging those who are ready with probing questions to make them think more deeply. We work hard to ensure that students enjoy their learning and want to do well.
In Year 9, students take a wide range of subjects and make their GCSE choices in the spring term. Parents are fully involved in this process. At GCSE all students study English Language, Mathematics, Science and can choose subjects from a wide range of options.
Most students will take 9 GCSEs, though some can opt for fewer, and many will take more. We report every half-term to parents on progress and how things are going in both classwork and prep.
Academic work is underpinned by a more general development of study skills and revision strategies. Students take exams relatively early in the year – so there is time to give them help to improve. We seek to embed a healthy attitude to work. There is a good deal of praise, and criticism is always diagnostic and supportive.
Students use a laptop for most of their work and they are given help in learning how to do this well. We use Google Classroom, which helps pupils organize their work and provides parents and guardians with a weekly summary of assignments.
All our teachers are experienced with, and supportive of, dyslexic students, students with ADHD and mild autism and this is reflected in the way they teach. Our Teaching and Learning Centre (TLC) guides both pupils and subject teachers in the most effective way to learn. We have some experience with other special educational needs too but everyone who joins the school must be able to complete GCSEs in most subjects.
LEX Futures and LEX Think
Year 9 students take part in a weekly carousel of activities designed to teach them employability skills. They take part in a Business Challenge, debating and critical thinking, learning about teamwork, collaboration and communication.
Years 10 and 11 take part in LEX Think where they are academically enriched and extended beyond the curriculum.
The Tutor System
Clayesmore operates a successful and effective tutor system. Pupils have one tutor for Year 9, and new one for Year 10 and 11, the GCSE years.
Tutors act as a mentor for all their tutees and in this work are supported by Houseparents and Deputy Head (Academic). They will advise them on managing academic work, sorting out any problems which arise, choosing subjects for GCSEs or A Levels and generally being someone they can count on for good advice while they are at school.
Pupils will see their tutor briefly most days and have a longer Tutor group meeting every Friday afternoon. These are enjoyable moments in the weekly timetable and pupils make full use of this unique and helpful relationship.
Senior Academic Support
The Teaching and Learning Centre (TLC) provides specialist 1:1 and small group teaching to underpin the work that is done in classes. These lessons are provided for students who opt for one or two fewer subjects. They take place in the working day.
We place great importance on knowing the profile of individual pupils in order to teach to the strengths of each child, whilst working to improve and support them develop the underlying skills they need to become independent learners. After specialist assessment, targets are set, in consultation with pupils and parents, for lessons within the Teaching and Learning Centre and classroom strategies are shared across the school.
In addition to specialist dyslexic support, we support some students with the development of speech and language skills, social skills, fine and gross motor skills. We encourage all students, should they need to do so, to use assistive technology, such as dictation software, within the Prep and Senior Schools. The whole school is accredited by CReSTeD.

Beyond the Classroom
Co-Curricular Opportunities for Years 9–11
At Clayesmore, education goes beyond the classroom. Our co-curricular programme for Years 9–11 is designed to complement academic learning, helping pupils develop skills, confidence, and character that prepare them for higher education, careers, and life beyond school.
All Senior School pupils take part in LEX on Saturdays, our flagship programme offering a wide range of practical, engaging, and skills-based activities. From forensics, robotics, and flight training to TEFL, referee and umpiring qualifications, first aid, self-defence, and outdoor adventures, pupils gain recognised qualifications while building leadership, teamwork, problem-solving, and communication skills.
LEX Futures in Years 9 supports careers and personal development through business challenges, debate, critical thinking, and service projects, helping pupils explore potential careers while developing resilience, purpose, and employability skills. Pupils also have opportunities to volunteer in the community, take part in the Model United Nations, and complete the Duke of Edinburgh’s Award, fostering independence, social responsibility, and global awareness.
Creative and performing arts are celebrated at Clayesmore. Pupils can learn an instrument, join the choir, ensembles, or bands, and participate in a school theatre production, whether on stage or backstage, developing creativity, collaboration, and confidence.
For Year 11, LEX Think sessions provide focused support for examinations, enhancing critical thinking and analytical skills. Across all activities, pupils also gain career-ready skills, from CV writing and interview techniques to entrepreneurship, ensuring they leave school academically capable, personally confident, and ready to thrive in a rapidly changing world.
With its breadth, variety, and emphasis on personal growth, adventure, creativity, and global engagement, Clayesmore’s co-curricular programme is a unique complement to academic excellence, giving pupils experiences that last a lifetime.
